name: toolbar
title: Toolbar
summary: Holds a set of related controls — actions, toggles, a choice among a few, a menu — as one Tab stop: inline where its content needs it (an editor's formatting bar, a table's actions, a row of filters), docked across an edge of the screen or of a region, or floating over the content.

anatomy.description: The surface that holds the items: none of its own in the default system where the toolbar stands inline in the content; a bar across the bottom edge of the screen whose color reaches under the bottom system inset (docked); or a rounded, raised surface over the content (floating).

The controls, in reading order: the product's own Tanrei Buttons, icon-only and labelled, toggles among them, Buttons that open a Menu, and Buttons with menu, alone or in groups. The toolbar lays them out and moves keyboard focus among them; it does not restyle them.
A line across the toolbar between two groups, or where a separator item stands, or the empty space that takes its place, as the design system's separation says.
The icon-only Button at the end that opens a Menu of the items that do not fit, drawn only while some do not.
The docked toolbar's top edge, or the edge around a floating or an inline toolbar's whole shape (none in the default system for the last two).

props.name: variant
props.description: Inline stands in place where the layout puts it, as long as its items need and no longer than the layout allows, with no surface, shadow or edge of its own in the default system (an editor's formatting bar, a table's actions, a row of filters); docked is a full-width bar along the bottom edge of the screen, flush with it; floating is a rounded, raised surface over the content, as long as its items. One product places a toolbar inside its content on one screen, docks it on another and floats it on a third. A design system may add values.

props.name: orientation
props.description: The direction the items run. Vertical is for an inline or a floating toolbar beside the content (a floating one on a large screen); a docked toolbar is always horizontal.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the toolbar for assistive technology ("Formatting", "Message actions"). Never drawn. Required.

props.name: overflow
props.description: What happens when the items do not fit along the toolbar's axis: menu hides items from the end into an overflow menu at the end of the toolbar (TBR-18); scroll keeps every item and scrolls them (TBR-8).

props.name: overflowLabel
props.description: The overflow button's accessible name ("More actions"), in the product's language. Never drawn. Empty takes the product's words. Needed whenever the toolbar may be narrower than its items.

props.name: separation
props.description: How two groups, or a separator item, set items apart: divider draws a line across the toolbar with space on each side, gap leaves empty space and no line. Auto takes comp.toolbar.separation, the design system's answer (divider in the default system).

items.name: action
items.summary: An icon action: a Button of the text variant and the medium size with an icon and no label, unless the product sets otherwise, laid out by the toolbar and not restyled; a toggle (bold, mute) is one with toggle set.

props.name: label
props.description: Its accessible name ("Bold"), as the Button's label. Required.

props.name: variant
props.description: As the Button's variant: text for most actions, filled for the one the toolbar leads to (Done, Send).

props.name: toggle
props.description: As the Button's toggle: the action switches something on and off.

props.name: selected
props.description: As the Button's selected: whether a toggle is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: As the Button's disabled.

props.name: overflow
props.description: Whether the toolbar may hide this item into its overflow menu when space runs out: never keeps it (Send, Done). Read by the toolbar to place the item.

slots.name: icon
slots.description: Its glyph, as the Button's icon slot. A fixture item's content is this glyph.

events.name: click
events.description: The action was activated, as the Button's click.

events.name: change
events.description: A toggle was switched, as the Button's change.

items.name: button
items.summary: A labelled action: the button component, medium unless the product sets otherwise, laid out by the toolbar and not restyled.

props.name: variant
props.description: As the button's variant.

props.name: toggle
props.description: As the button's toggle: a labelled toggle (a filter that is on or off).

props.name: selected
props.description: As the button's selected: whether a toggle is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: As the button's disabled.

props.name: overflow
props.description: Whether the toolbar may hide this item into its overflow menu when space runs out: never keeps it (Send, Done). Read by the toolbar to place the item.

slots.name: default
slots.description: Its label, as the button's default slot. A fixture item's content is this label.

events.name: click
events.description: The button was activated, as the button's click.

events.name: change
events.description: A toggle was switched, as the button's change.

items.name: menu-button
items.summary: A Button that opens a Tanrei Menu anchored to it (Sort, Insert): icon-only unless the product sets otherwise, laid out by the toolbar as any other item and not restyled. The Menu is the product's, beside it in the toolbar; it is neither laid out nor an item.

props.name: label
props.description: Its accessible name ("Sort"), as the Button's label. Required.

props.name: variant
props.description: As the Button's variant.

props.name: disabled
props.description: As the Button's disabled.

props.name: overflow
props.description: Whether the toolbar may hide this item into its overflow menu when space runs out: never keeps it (Send, Done). Read by the toolbar to place the item.

slots.name: icon
slots.description: Its glyph, as the Button's icon slot. A fixture item's content is this glyph.

events.name: click
events.description: The button was activated, as the Button's click: the product opens its Menu.

items.name: button-with-menu
items.summary: A Button with menu: a main action and a menu of related ones, each half a stop of the toolbar's arrow keys (TBR-25), laid out by the toolbar and not restyled.

props.name: label
props.description: The leading half's label ("Save"), as the Button with menu's label.

props.name: menuLabel
props.description: The trailing half's accessible name ("More save options"), as the Button with menu's menuLabel.

props.name: variant
props.description: As the Button with menu's variant.

props.name: disabled
props.description: As the Button with menu's disabled.

props.name: overflow
props.description: Whether the toolbar may hide this item into its overflow menu when space runs out: never keeps it (Send, Done). Read by the toolbar to place the item.

events.name: click
events.description: The main action was activated, as the Button with menu's click.

events.name: toggle
events.description: The trailing half asks to open or close the menu, as the Button with menu's toggle.

items.name: group
items.summary: A run of related items (Bold, Italic, Underline), optionally named; the toolbar sets it apart from what is next to it as separation says. It draws nothing of its own.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the group for assistive technology ("Text style"); never drawn. Empty leaves the group unexposed: its items are the toolbar's.

items.name: separator
items.summary: A line across the toolbar between two items outside the groups: the toolbar draws it as it draws the line between two groups, and it is never a stop of the arrow keys.

slots.name: default
slots.description: Holds the items, in reading order: Tanrei Buttons, icon-only and labelled, Buttons with a Tanrei Menu anchored to them (the Menu beside its Button), Buttons with menu, groups of them and separators.

behavior.text: WHILE variant is docked THE toolbar SHALL span the full width of its parent, be at least comp.toolbar.container.size.docked high above the bottom system inset, fill its container with comp.toolbar.container.color.docked, raise it by comp.toolbar.container.elevation.docked, round it by comp.toolbar.container.shape.docked, and draw its top edge comp.toolbar.outline.width thick in comp.toolbar.outline.color.docked.
behavior.verify: Docked fixtures are drawn in a 360 × 64 stage (the toolbar across its width, no system inset).

behavior.text: WHILE variant is docked THE toolbar SHALL lay its items out in one row in reading order, the first comp.toolbar.container.padding-inline.docked from the start edge and the last as far from the end edge, with equal space between neighbours and never less than comp.toolbar.container.gap.docked, each item vertically centered in the row; a toolbar with one item SHALL center it.

WHILE variant is docked THE toolbar SHALL extend its container under the bottom system inset (home indicator, gesture bar, taskbar) and SHALL place its items above that inset and inside the left and right insets, so that its color reaches the screen's bottom edge while no item sits under a system bar.

WHILE variant is floating THE toolbar SHALL fill its container with comp.toolbar.container.color.floating, raise it by comp.toolbar.container.elevation.floating, round it by comp.toolbar.container.shape.floating eased by sys.shape.corner-smoothing, draw an edge comp.toolbar.outline.width thick in comp.toolbar.outline.color.floating around its whole shape, be as long along its axis as its items need — comp.toolbar.container.padding-inline.floating at each end and comp.toolbar.container.gap.floating between neighbours, or as much more as TBR-16 keeps for their targets — and at least comp.toolbar.container.size.floating across it, with every item centered across the axis.
behavior.verify: Horizontal floating fixtures are drawn centered in a 360 × 96 stage, so that the elevation's shadow shows on every side.

behavior.text: WHILE variant is floating THE toolbar SHALL NOT position itself: it SHALL lay out at its own size where the layout that holds it places it (normally centered above the bottom edge of the content, clear of a navigation bar and of the system inset, or beside the content's end edge for a vertical toolbar), and SHALL NOT draw a scrim, move content or reach under a system inset.

WHILE orientation is vertical and variant is floating or inline THE toolbar SHALL stack its items from top to bottom in the order given, with its variant's paddings and gap along the vertical axis and at least its variant's container size as its width; WHILE orientation is vertical and variant is docked THE toolbar SHALL lay out as a horizontal docked toolbar and in debug builds report that a docked toolbar is horizontal.
behavior.verify: The vertical fixture is drawn centered in a 96 × 240 stage.

behavior.text: WHEN the layout direction is right-to-left THE toolbar SHALL lay out a horizontal toolbar's items from the right edge, in reading order, mirrored; a vertical toolbar SHALL keep its top-to-bottom order.

WHILE overflow is scroll and the items need more length than the toolbar has along its axis THE toolbar SHALL keep every item at its own size and the gap at its minimum, SHALL scroll its items along its axis so that every item stays reachable, and SHALL bring an item that receives keyboard focus fully into view; it SHALL NOT wrap, shrink or hide an item.

THE toolbar SHALL NOT restyle its items: each SHALL render as the Button it is, from its own tokens, variant and size, and SHALL keep its own press, focus, target and disabled behaviour and its own semantics, a toggle Button staying a toggle. Between two items the hit areas SHALL never overlap (as BGR-4): in a docked toolbar they SHALL meet at the middle of the gap, and in a floating or an inline one where the lengths TBR-16 keeps for the two items meet; each item SHALL keep its full target on every side that has no neighbour. In a docked toolbar the gap (at least comp.toolbar.container.gap.docked) is what keeps an item's target whole between its neighbours: at sys.target.touch minus the item's length or more, every item keeps its full target there, as the default system's gap does for every Button size; a layer that narrows that gap narrows the targets between items. In a floating or an inline toolbar TBR-16 keeps it, whatever comp.toolbar.container.gap.floating or comp.toolbar.container.gap.inline is.
behavior.verify: Under the default system comp.toolbar.container.gap.docked is 16, sys.target.touch (48) minus the small icon-only Button (32), comp.toolbar.container.gap.floating is 0, and comp.toolbar.container.padding-inline.floating is 12, the space across the row around a medium item ((64 − 40) / 2), more than its reach (4): in floating, floating-filled-action, floating-vertical and the docked fixtures every item's hit area is at least 48 along the axis and 48 across it, and Android's touch-target check (48 dp, an error for the default system) passes on each of them.

behavior.text: THE toolbar SHALL be one Tab stop: the item that had keyboard focus last, or else the first item that is not disabled. Its items are its own and its groups' items, in reading order; a separator and a Menu anchored to an item are none. WHILE an item has keyboard focus, Right Arrow and Left Arrow in a horizontal toolbar (Left Arrow moving to the next item in a right-to-left layout) and Down Arrow and Up Arrow in a vertical one SHALL move focus to the next and previous item that is not disabled, wrapping at the ends, and Home and End to the first and last such item; moving focus SHALL NOT activate an item, and Enter and Space SHALL act on the focused item as that item does. A disabled item SHALL NOT take focus, as its own spec says (BTN-2).

THE toolbar SHALL expose itself as a toolbar named by label, with its orientation, on a platform that has a toolbar role, and on any other platform as a group named by label that contains its items in order; each item SHALL keep its own name, role and state, and the toolbar SHALL add nothing to them.

WHILE label is empty THE toolbar SHALL still render, and in debug builds report that it has no accessible name. IF the toolbar holds no item, or an element that is neither one of its item kinds nor a Menu anchored to one of its items, THE toolbar SHALL still lay it out, and in debug builds report it, because a field or a slider would take the arrow keys the toolbar moves focus with (the WAI-ARIA toolbar pattern).

WHEN variant names a value that the active design system does not have, or orientation a value the component does not define, THE toolbar SHALL render with the default value (inline, horizontal), and in debug builds report the unknown value. A variant value that a layer adds SHALL take the inline structure with its own values, because the structure is not a value a layer can set. WHEN overflow or separation names a value the component does not define THE toolbar SHALL render with menu or auto, and in debug builds report it.

WHILE the text size is enlarged THE toolbar SHALL grow across its axis to hold its items (its size is a minimum) and SHALL NOT scale its items itself; each item grows or keeps its size as its own spec says.

THE toolbar SHALL take its layout direction from where it is used — the direction of the nearest ancestor that sets one, and the platform's own where none does — and SHALL have no direction setting of its own; WHEN that direction changes while the toolbar is shown THE toolbar SHALL draw itself for the new direction at once, without a motion of its own, keeping its focus and the item its Tab stop stands on.
behavior.verify: Test with the direction set on an ancestor inside the page or the view tree, not on the root, and again changed after the first render. On the web the test is owed with the other right-to-left tests.

behavior.text: WHILE variant is floating THE toolbar SHALL lay its items comp.toolbar.container.gap.floating apart (and WHILE it is inline comp.toolbar.container.gap.inline apart, TBR-17), measured between their visible bounds along its axis, and SHALL move two neighbours further apart only as far as each needs in order to keep, centred on itself, a length of sys.target.touch along the axis that its neighbour's does not reach into, because items that stand this close cannot extend a hit area over each other (as BGR-3): where the token is 0, as in the default system, an item at least sys.target.touch long touches its neighbour, and a shorter one stands half of what it lacks away from it. THE toolbar SHALL NOT widen, resize or restyle an item to do so (TBR-9), SHALL space its items the same whatever the input type, so that the toolbar does not change with the pointer, and SHALL space them so along the vertical axis WHILE orientation is vertical (TBR-6). A floating toolbar is as long as its items need (TBR-4) and never spreads them across a width; WHILE variant is docked THE toolbar SHALL spread its items across its width and keep comp.toolbar.container.gap.docked as the least space between them (TBR-2), unchanged.
behavior.verify: Fixture floating under the default system: four medium icon-only Buttons (40) stand 8 apart (4 + 4) where they stood 16, and the toolbar is 208 long (4 × 40 + 3 × 8 + 2 × 12) where it was 232. floating-vertical: the same along the column. Unit: a floating toolbar of large (56) Buttons draws them touching; one of small (32) Buttons 16 apart; with sys.target.touch set to 0 in a test layer every size touches. The docked fixtures do not move.

behavior.text: WHILE variant is inline THE toolbar SHALL lay its items out in one line along its axis where the layout places it, as long as its items need and never longer than the layout allows, with comp.toolbar.container.padding-inline.inline at each end, comp.toolbar.container.gap.inline between neighbours spaced as TBR-16 spaces a floating toolbar's, and at least comp.toolbar.container.size.inline across its axis; it SHALL fill its container with comp.toolbar.container.color.inline, raise it by comp.toolbar.container.elevation.inline, round it by comp.toolbar.container.shape.inline and edge it comp.toolbar.outline.width thick in comp.toolbar.outline.color.inline (transparent, none and no edge in the default system), and SHALL NOT read a system inset, position itself or spread its items.
behavior.verify: Fixture inline-formatting under the default system: no fill, no shadow, no edge; 40 high; the first item at the start edge; two medium icon-only items 8 apart (the 4 + 4 their targets lack, more than the gap's 4).

behavior.text: WHILE overflow is menu and the items, at their own sizes and with the least gaps, need more length along the axis than the layout offers the toolbar — the length it would take with every item shown, which a parent as long as its content passes on from further up, so that it can grow while the toolbar and its parent stay as long as the items still shown — THE toolbar SHALL hide items from its end, in reverse reading order and one at a time, skipping every item whose overflow is never, until the items that remain and the overflow button fit; SHALL draw the overflow button after the last item that remains — an icon-only Tanrei Button of the text variant and the medium size, showing the glyph more_horiz in a horizontal toolbar and more_vert in a vertical one, named by overflowLabel or the product's words, exposed as a button that opens a menu, with its expanded state; and SHALL NOT hide an item whose overflow is never even when the items then do not fit, in which case TBR-8 applies to what remains.
behavior.verify: Fixture inline-overflow: eight items in a 240-wide stage; the items that fit and the overflow button, nothing past the stage's end. inline-overflow-pinned: Send stays and the items before it are hidden. The same toolbar in a parent as long as its content — an inline-block, a flex item, a float, an absolutely placed box — inside a 240-wide box: the items that fit; the box widened to 600: every item, in the frame after the widening; narrowed to 320: the items that fit again. rtl-inline-overflow: inline-overflow, from the right.

behavior.text: THE toolbar SHALL decide which items are hidden before the first frame in which it is drawn, and again in the frame in which its items or the length the layout offers it (TBR-18) change, so that no item is drawn and then hidden in a later frame, and its size across its axis never changes because an item was hidden or shown; hiding and showing items SHALL NOT be animated, because it answers a change of the layout that a motion would lag behind.

WHEN the overflow button is activated THE toolbar SHALL open a Tanrei Menu anchored to it, placed bottom-end (in a vertical toolbar, at the side away from the edge it stands at), holding the hidden items in reading order: an action or a labelled Button as a menu item with its label and its icon, disabled while it is; a toggle as a checkbox item with its selected state; a menu button as a submenu item holding its menu's items; a Button with menu as an item for its main action followed by a submenu item named by its menuLabel; and a separator, or the boundary between two groups, as the menu's separation. Activating a menu item SHALL do exactly what activating the hidden item does — the same click or change, once, from that item — and close the menu.

WHEN the item that is the toolbar's Tab stop, or has keyboard focus, is hidden THE toolbar SHALL make the overflow button the Tab stop and, if focus was on the item, move focus to the overflow button; THE overflow button SHALL be the last stop of the arrow-key order (TBR-10).

THE toolbar SHALL lay out a group's items in its own line, in place, as items of the toolbar (the group draws nothing of its own), SHALL expose a group whose label is not empty as a group named by that label, and a group whose label is empty as nothing (its items are the toolbar's).

THE toolbar SHALL set two neighbouring groups — or a group and an item outside any group — apart as separation names: WHILE it is divider by a line comp.toolbar.divider.thickness thick and comp.toolbar.divider.length long across the axis, centred, in comp.toolbar.divider.color, with comp.toolbar.group.gap on each side; WHILE it is gap by twice comp.toolbar.group.gap of empty space. A separator item SHALL be drawn the same way wherever it stands. THE toolbar SHALL expose each such line as a separator, SHALL never make it a stop of the arrow keys, and SHALL draw no line at the start or the end of the toolbar, and never two lines side by side.
behavior.verify: Fixture inline-formatting under the default system: a line 1 thick and 24 long in outline-variant, 8 from the items on each side. inline-separation-gap: 16 of empty space and no line.

behavior.text: WHILE an item is the anchor of a Menu THE toolbar SHALL keep it an item of the arrow-key order and SHALL neither lay out nor count the Menu; WHILE that Menu is open its keys SHALL be the Menu's, and WHEN it closes focus SHALL return to its anchor, which stays the Tab stop.
THE toolbar SHALL make each half of a Button with menu a stop of its own in the arrow-key order, the leading half first in reading order, each keeping its own name, role and state.

keyboard.action: Moves focus into the toolbar (to the item focused last, or the first enabled item) and out of it: the toolbar is one Tab stop.

keyboard.keys: Right Arrow / Left Arrow (horizontal), Down Arrow / Up Arrow (vertical)
keyboard.action: Moves focus to the next or previous enabled item — a group's items and each half of a Button with menu included, separators skipped, the overflow button last — wrapping at the ends (Left and Right mirrored in right-to-left layouts).
Moves focus to the first or last enabled item.
Activates the focused item, as that Button does; on the overflow button, opens the menu of the hidden items.

accessibility.labeling: label names the toolbar; it is never drawn. A group's label names the group; empty leaves it unexposed. Each item is named by its own label (an icon-only Button's label, a labelled Button's text), and the overflow button by overflowLabel or the product's words. The toolbar adds no name, role or state to its items.
notes: The toolbar has no target of its own and takes no input: its items are the product's Buttons, icon-only and labelled, which meet the minimum target themselves (BTN-5). A medium item's target (48) fits inside a floating toolbar's 64, and reaches past an inline toolbar's 40 as a Button's does anywhere.

The web has the toolbar role (with aria-orientation) and React Native has role toolbar. SwiftUI, Compose and Flutter have no toolbar role: there the toolbar is a group (an accessibility container, a traversal group, a semantics container) named by label, and each README says so.
One Tab stop with arrow-key movement is the WAI-ARIA toolbar pattern. It uses the same roving focus the list, menu and tabs use on each platform; a Button outside a toolbar is unchanged.

A toolbar holds Buttons, menu buttons, Buttons with menu, groups of them and separators. Anything else is laid out and reported (TBR-12), because a control that uses the arrow keys would take the keys the toolbar moves focus with.
A docked toolbar and a navigation bar are not used on the same screen: both claim the bottom edge.
How the items look is their own design system's answer; the toolbar reads no state tokens.
Hidden items stay reachable: the overflow button is the last stop of the arrow keys, and its menu holds every hidden item with its own name and state; activating one is activating the item.

web.name: tanrei-toolbar
web.notes: The items are `<tanrei-button>` children, icon-only and labelled, `<tanrei-button-with-menu>` children, `<tanrei-toolbar-group>` children holding them, and `<tanrei-divider>` separators; a `<tanrei-menu anchor>` child anchored to an item's id is that item's Menu and is not laid out. The host has `role="toolbar"`, `aria-orientation` and `aria-label` from `label`; a group with a label has `role="group"` and `aria-label`. The toolbar assigns each of its children, and a group each of its items, to a slot of its own (manual slot assignment), so that the toolbar draws the separations between them and leaves a hidden item unassigned: a hidden item is not drawn and keeps its place, its listeners and its state in the page. The overflow button and its menu are elements of the toolbar's shadow root. The roving Tab stop sets `tabindex` on the item elements (0 on the Tab stop, -1 on the others): an item delegates focus to the button in its shadow root, and a host whose tabindex is -1 takes that button out of the Tab order; a Button with menu is told which of its halves is the Tab stop through the internal channel (SPB-33). A docked toolbar's bottom inset is `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`. Snapshot harness: the stages of TBR-1, TBR-4, TBR-6 and TBR-18.

action.name: tanrei-button
action.notes: An icon-only `<tanrei-button>` child; the glyph is its content.

button.name: tanrei-button
button.notes: A `<tanrei-button>` child; the label is its content.

menu-button.name: tanrei-button
menu-button.notes: A `<tanrei-button id>` child with a `<tanrei-menu anchor="<its id>">` beside it, in the toolbar or in the same group.

button-with-menu.name: tanrei-button-with-menu
button-with-menu.notes: A `<tanrei-button-with-menu>` child, its menu items in `slot="menu"` as anywhere.

group.name: tanrei-toolbar-group
group.notes: A `<tanrei-toolbar-group>` child holding items: `display: contents`, with `role="group"` and `aria-label` while its label is not empty.

separator.name: tanrei-divider
separator.notes: A `<tanrei-divider>` child: the toolbar draws the line itself, as between two groups (TBR-23), as an element of its own with `role="separator"`, and leaves the divider unassigned.

swiftui.name: TanreiToolbar
swiftui.notes: `TanreiToolbar(_ label: String, variant:, orientation:) { items }`, a view builder of `TanreiButton`s, icon-only and labelled. A docked toolbar is placed with `.safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom)`, its background ignoring the bottom safe area. SwiftUI's own `.toolbar` with a bottom-bar placement is not used: its bar cannot take the tokens. SwiftUI has no toolbar role: the toolbar is an accessibility container (`.accessibilityElement(children: .contain)`) labelled by `label`. The roving Tab stop is one focus group for the keyboard: Full Keyboard Access moves among its items with the arrow keys and leaves it with Tab. Lagging: the inline variant, the overflow menu, groups, separators, menu buttons and Buttons with menu as items are not built on this platform yet; it draws the docked and floating toolbar of icon-only and labelled Buttons, docked by default. `.toolbarOverflow(.never)` on an item keeps it; the overflow menu is a SwiftUI `Menu` drawn from the Tanrei Menu's tokens.

action.name: TanreiButton
action.notes: An icon-only `TanreiButton` in the toolbar's view builder; a toggle is its `isSelected:` initializer.

button.name: TanreiButton
button.notes: A `TanreiButton` in the toolbar's view builder.

menu-button.name: TanreiButton
menu-button.notes: A `TanreiButton` with `.tanreiMenu { … }` attached, in the toolbar's view builder.

button-with-menu.name: TanreiButtonWithMenu
button-with-menu.notes: A `TanreiButtonWithMenu` in the toolbar's view builder.

group.name: TanreiToolbarGroup
group.notes: `TanreiToolbarGroup(_ label:) { items }` in the toolbar's view builder: an accessibility container named by its label, or none without one.

separator.name: TanreiDivider
separator.notes: A `TanreiDivider()` in the toolbar's view builder; the toolbar draws the line from its own tokens.

compose.name: TanreiToolbar
compose.notes: `TanreiToolbar(contentDescription, modifier, variant, orientation, windowInsets) { … }`, the items called in its content lambda. `windowInsets` defaults to `WindowInsets.navigationBars` for a docked toolbar and to none for a floating one. Compose has no toolbar role: the toolbar is a traversal group (`isTraversalGroup`) labelled by `contentDescription`, and the README says so. The roving Tab stop is `TanreiRovingFocus`, the primitive the list, menu and tabs use, horizontal or vertical by orientation; the toolbar registers each item it holds. Lagging: the inline variant, the overflow menu, groups, separators, menu buttons and Buttons with menu as items are not built on this platform yet; it draws the docked and floating toolbar of icon-only and labelled Buttons, docked by default. `Modifier.toolbarOverflow(TanreiToolbarOverflow.Never)` on an item keeps it; the overflow menu is a `TanreiMenu`.

action.name: TanreiButton
action.notes: An icon-only `TanreiButton` called in the toolbar's content lambda.

button.name: TanreiButton
button.notes: A `TanreiButton` called in the toolbar's content lambda.

menu-button.name: TanreiButton
menu-button.notes: A `TanreiButton` with a `TanreiMenu` anchored to it, called in the toolbar's content lambda.

button-with-menu.name: TanreiButtonWithMenu
button-with-menu.notes: A `TanreiButtonWithMenu` called in the toolbar's content lambda.

group.name: TanreiToolbarGroup
group.notes: `TanreiToolbarGroup(contentDescription) { … }` in the toolbar's content lambda: a traversal group named by its description, or none without one.

separator.name: TanreiDivider
separator.notes: A `TanreiDivider()` called in the toolbar's content lambda; the toolbar draws the line from its own tokens.

flutter.name: TanreiToolbar
flutter.notes: `TanreiToolbar(semanticLabel:, variant:, orientation:, children: [...])` (`orientation` is Flutter's `Axis`). A docked toolbar applies the bottom `MediaQuery.padding` itself, as `SafeArea` would, with its color under it. Flutter's widgets library has no toolbar role: the toolbar is a `Semantics(container: true, explicitChildNodes: true, label:)`, and the README says so. The roving Tab stop is `TanreiItemGroupMixin`, the primitive the list, menu and tabs use, with its item axis set by orientation. Lagging: the inline variant, the overflow menu, groups, separators, menu buttons and Buttons with menu as items are not built on this platform yet; it draws the docked and floating toolbar of icon-only and labelled Buttons, docked by default. An item wrapped in `TanreiToolbarItem(overflow: TanreiToolbarOverflow.never, child:)` is kept; the overflow menu is a `TanreiMenu`.

menu-button.name: TanreiButton
menu-button.notes: A `TanreiButton` that opens a `TanreiMenu` anchored to it, in the toolbar's `children`.

group.name: TanreiToolbarGroup
group.notes: `TanreiToolbarGroup(semanticLabel:, children:)` in the toolbar's `children`: a semantics container named by its label, or none without one.

separator.name: TanreiDivider
separator.notes: A `TanreiDivider()` in the toolbar's `children`; the toolbar draws the line from its own tokens.

react-native.name: Toolbar
react-native.notes: `<Toolbar variant orientation accessibilityLabel insets>{items}</Toolbar>`, the items being `Button` elements, icon-only and labelled. The view has `role="toolbar"`. A docked toolbar takes the bottom inset from its own `insets` prop, falling back to `TanreiProvider`'s `insets`; the package takes no safe-area dependency. The roving Tab stop and the arrow keys work where a hardware keyboard is attached, as the tabs row's do. Lagging: the inline variant, the overflow menu, groups, separators, menu buttons and Buttons with menu as items are not built on this platform yet; it draws the docked and floating toolbar of icon-only and labelled Buttons, docked by default. `toolbarOverflow="never"` on an item keeps it; the overflow menu is a `Menu`.

action.name: Button
action.notes: An icon-only `Button` element among the toolbar's children.

button.name: Button
button.notes: A `Button` element among the toolbar's children.

menu-button.name: Button
menu-button.notes: A `Button` with a `Menu` anchored to it, among the toolbar's children.

group.name: ToolbarGroup

separator.name: Divider
